newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot electricity steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot electricity steady to lower.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast were steady to lower Monday against Friday's levels amid a lack of transactions due to cool weather, market sources said.
Although natural gas prices rose today, modest electricity demand in the region overrode concerns about a slight pickup in marginal generation costs today, traders said.
"We've been maxing our gas resources," said a Northeast utility official, adding fuel oil was still much more costly than natural gas.
With the exception of those taken off line for maintenance and/or refueling, most baseload generating plants were operating, market sources said.

Boston Edison Co's 670 MW Pilgrim nuclear station in Plymouth, Mass., restarted this past weekend after being shut two weeks ago due to a saltwater intrusion in a set of heat exchangers in its reactor building.
For Tuesday, peak, non-firm electricity in the western New York Power Pool (NYPP) was quoted $16.00-$18.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Friday's $19.00-$20.00 range for Monday.
Tuesday's off-peak power prices in western NYPP were discussed at $9.00-$13.00, unchanged from Friday's levels.
Non-firm power prices for heavy load hours on Tuesday in eastern NYPP were assessed at $21.00-$22.00 per MWh, lower than a quote of $23.00-$24.00 on Friday.
Tuesday's off-peak electricity in the eastern portion of NYPP was valued at $14.00-$15.00, flat from Friday.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), non-firm power during peak hours on Tuesday was offered at $30.00-$34.00 with few deals done, compared with Friday's range of $26.00-$28.00 for Monday.
Tuesday's non-firm, off-peak electricity prices in NEPOOL was discussed at $21.00-$22.00, versus a quote of $22.00 on Friday for Monday power.
The latest forecasts showed temperatures in most of the Northeast to be above-normal next week.
